title: Coherent localized derived scalar extension and comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme and phi:B -> Bprime a homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings. There exist coherent localized derived functors T on the etale site and S on the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-presheaves], whose global and slice functors are left adjoints to the actual derived restriction-of-scalars functors. There is a comparison isomorphism nu^* followed by S.global isomorphic to T.global followed by nu^* [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-sheaf-comparison]. Its mate is normalized by the comparison unit equation; the local comparisons are normalized by both slice unit equations. For every actual etale-local derived map f, comparison after T maps f to the same map as S after comparison, conjugated by the global comparison and slice isomorphisms. The precise three unit equations and actual-local-map equation are the attached Lean statement. No finite ring, boundedness or Tor-dimension assumption is made.

proof.text: Construct global and slice extension-of-scalars functors by resolving with K-flat flat-term complexes and applying sheafified tensor extension. The derived adjunction to exact restriction of scalars follows from the ordinary tensor-restriction adjunction. This works for arbitrary commutative rings and all unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 0G7E, derived pullback on K-flat flat-term representatives

proof.text: Restriction to a slice and comparison inverse image preserve K-flat flat-term complexes. The ordinary balancing maps of tensor extension therefore compute the derived comparisons. On pure tensors they send a section to the same restricted or pulled-back tensor; the reverse balancing map is the inverse. Composition of pullbacks gives all coherence identities. These maps define the restrictionIso fields and hom_naturality and iso_naturality of both DerivedLocalFunctor structures. Fix each comparison as the adjunction transpose of the restricted global unit followed by the inverse canonical restriction-of-scalars comparison. Its naturality follows from unit naturality; the inverse law of the hom equivalence gives the slice unit equation. On flat resolutions this same mate is the balancing isomorphism, so the chosen canonical mate is invertible.

The ordinary unit is m -> 1 tensor m. Its equality under each balancing map gives the two slice unit equations and the global comparison unit equation. Both routes on an actual localized derived morphism use its tensor-extension chain map and the same balancing comparisons. The chain-map equality descends to the final displayed Hom-presheaf equality. Functors carry isomorphisms to inverse pairs, so this suffices for both Hom and Isom consumers. To identify the derived units with the chain-level ones, compose the derived unit with restriction of the left-derived counit: the derived-adjunction factorization formula gives the localized ordinary unit followed by the exact restriction localization comparison. Mates paste compatibly for successive restrictions, which proves that the conjugated actual-map squares use precisely the displayed canonical maps.

theorem derivedScalarExtension_localSystems
    (B' : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing B'] (φ : B →+* B') :
    ∃ T : DerivedLocalFunctor X.smallEtaleTopology B B',
    ∃ S : DerivedLocalFunctor (ProEt.topology X) B B',
    ∃ c : derivedComparison X B ⋙ S.globalFunctor ≅
      T.globalFunctor ⋙ derivedComparison X B',
      ∃ aT : T.globalFunctor ⊣ Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology φ,
      ∃ aS : S.globalFunctor ⊣ Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars (ProEt.topology X) φ,
      ∃ aTL : ∀ V : X.Etale, T.localFunctor V ⊣
        Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars (X.smallEtaleTopology.over V) φ,
      ∃ aSL : ∀ U : X.ProEt, S.localFunctor U ⊣
        Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars ((ProEt.topology X).over U) φ,
      (∀ (A : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)))
        (V : X.Etale),
        (aTL V).unit.app ((derivedSliceRestriction X.smallEtaleTopology B V).obj A) ≫
            (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars (X.smallEtaleTopology.over V) φ).map
              ((T.restrictionIso V).hom.app A) ≫
            (sliceRestrictScalarsIso X.smallEtaleTopology B φ V).hom.app
              (T.globalFunctor.obj A) =
          (derivedSliceRestriction X.smallEtaleTopology B V).map (aT.unit.app A)) ∧
      (∀ (A : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)))
        (U : X.ProEt),
        (aSL U).unit.app ((derivedSliceRestriction (ProEt.topology X) B U).obj A) ≫
            (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars ((ProEt.topology X).over U) φ).map
              ((S.restrictionIso U).hom.app A) ≫
            (sliceRestrictScalarsIso (ProEt.topology X) B φ U).hom.app
              (S.globalFunctor.obj A) =
          (derivedSliceRestriction (ProEt.topology X) B U).map (aS.unit.app A)) ∧
      (∀ A : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)),
        aS.unit.app ((derivedComparison X B).obj A) ≫
            (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars (ProEt.topology X) φ).map (c.hom.app A) =
          (derivedComparison X B).map (aT.unit.app A) ≫
            (comparisonRestrictScalarsIso X B φ).hom.app (T.globalFunctor.obj A)) ∧
      (∀ (A D : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)))
        (V : X.Etale)
        (f : (derivedSliceRestriction X.smallEtaleTopology B V).obj A ⟶
          (derivedSliceRestriction X.smallEtaleTopology B V).obj D),
        derivedComparisonLocalHom X B' (T.globalFunctor.obj A) (T.globalFunctor.obj D) V
            ((T.homPresheafMap A D).app (op V) f) =
          (S.homPresheafMap ((derivedComparison X B).obj A)
              ((derivedComparison X B).obj D) ≫
            derivedLocalHomPresheafMap (c.inv.app A) (c.hom.app D)).app
              (op ((toProEt X).obj V)) (derivedComparisonLocalHom X B A D V f))
